column1: # Where each signing key is PUBLISHED, independently of the signature it makes.
# Read by tools/verify-signatures.sh, which fetches each key from the locator
# recorded here rather than asking a keyserver for the id a signature named.
# THE DISTINCTION THIS FILE EXISTS FOR.
#   DISCOVERY may be circular. Asking a keyserver for the key id a signature
#   names is how you find out which address to look up. It establishes nothing:
#   it proves a file was signed by whoever signed it.
#   CONFIRMATION must not be. A fingerprint earns a row here only when some
#   publisher states it by a route that does not depend on the signature, and
#   the row records exactly which route and when it was walked.
# Columns are whitespace separated; the note runs to the end of the line.
#   fingerprint  the full 40-character primary key fingerprint, uppercase
#   kind         korg | wkd | github | savannah
#   locator      kind korg: the URL the armoured key was fetched from
#                kind wkd:  the email address whose Web Key Directory serves it
#                kind github: https://github.com/<account>.gpg
#                kind savannah: the project's release-gpgkeys.php?group=<project>&download=1
#   retrieved    the date the confirmation was walked
#   signs        comma-separated source names this key signs, no spaces
#   note         the uid as published, and anything a reader needs
# What each kind establishes, precisely:
#   korg  git.kernel.org/pub/scm/docs/kernel/pgpkeys.git, whose README states
#         its purpose as distributing "Linux kernel developer PGP keys that
#         have valid trust paths to Linus Torvalds", one armoured key per long
#         key id. A match means kernel.org publishes THIS EXACT KEY for a
#         developer of that name.
#   wkd   the Web Key Directory of the signer's own email domain, served over
#         HTTPS by that domain. A match means that domain publishes this key
#         for that address. It is a third party's statement about the key and
#         is not upstream designating a release signer.
#   savannah  the release keyring GNU Savannah serves for the project, kept by
#         its maintainers. A match means the project's own forge lists THIS KEY
#         as one of its release signers.
#   github  the key GitHub publishes for a named account, AND that account is
#         the one that published the release we pin - checked through the
#         releases API and recorded in the note. This only ever applies to a
#         release whose tarball GitHub itself serves: the platform is already
#         the delivery channel, so taking the key from the same platform adds
#         no single point of failure that the download did not already have.
#         BE CLEAR ABOUT THE LIMIT: an attacker holding that GitHub account
#         breaks both halves at once. What it does establish is that the
#         fingerprint was not learned from the signature under test - it came
#         from the account that publishes the releases.
# NONE IS OUT-OF-BAND CONFIRMATION. All three rest on TLS and the CA system, and
# no human here has checked any of these fingerprints through a second channel.
# They are strictly better than a keyserver lookup by the id under test, and
# strictly weaker than a fingerprint Kryptik chose in advance - which is what
# PINNED_FPRS in tools/verify-signatures.sh is for.
# ADDING A ROW: walk the confirmation yourself and put the route in locator.
# Do not copy a fingerprint out of a distribution's package metadata or a blog
# post. If the publisher later serves a DIFFERENT key for the same locator,
# verify-signatures.sh treats that as a finding: it refuses the key and fails
# every source the row signs, held copy or not, because a silently rotated key
# is the case this file has to be able to notice. When upstream retires a key
# on purpose, its row goes, and the new key gets a row of its own.
# fingerprint                               kind  locator                                                                                      retrieved   signs             note
